correctness.rationale: Define Q=2^p-1 and c=1/(4Q). The p orbit points have distinct integer numerators 1, 2, 4, ..., 2^(p-1). The confidence set has three positive bands for p>=3 (long block 2 through 2^(p-2), singleton bands at 2^(p-1) and Q-1) and their reflections plus a central band. Inclusions are padded c, while each excluded stubborn distance is separated at least 3c. Consequently exactly the right stubborn opinion is trusted at each stage. R(x)=(x+1)/2 followed by p-1 halvings closes the orbit. Any initial difference of magnitude <c/2 is halved each step by induction; return multiplier 2^-p. For at most two agents the symmetric reciprocal-trust dichotomy or strict contraction toward a single stubborn opinion excludes nonconstant periodic states. Exact rational verifier from the delivered package checks periods 2..120 and perturbed trajectories; the infinite theorem is justified algebraically, not extrapolated from finite tests.

originality.rationale: The claimed all-integer prescribed prime periods with at most seven intervals, three agents and an explicit open attracting basin were compared at the implication level, not by title. The initiating full text contains only a specific three-agent period-three counterexample (Example 4), and its convergence theorem assumes homogeneous stubborn opinions. The general contraction results constrain the number of periodic orbits, not their least periods, and do not enforce the reciprocal SCOD trust geometry. Six actual published-finding corpus semantic searches and available published-claim searches did not identify a stronger or equivalent statement. The period-three existence claim is attributed, not claimed new. The positive originality judgment is best-knowledge and retains explicit specialized-priority risk.
residual_risks: Prior SCOD paper already gives period three; this finding must not be characterized as discovering periodicity with two stubborn agents.

value.rationale: The originating SCOD literature isolates the analytic risk of two distinct stubborn opinions and exhibits a period-three orbit. Establishing unbounded prime periods while keeping BOTH the population and the confidence-set component count fixed identifies a stronger structural limit to any convergence/finite-period classification. An explicitly attracting open initial-condition interval makes the construction dynamical rather than just a fragile periodic point. This is an infinite-family result directly motivated by the source and not an arbitrary table slice; the minimum population size is exact.
